subject: FinLytics integration - embed/reranker 5xx errors (post-call follow-up)
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: FinLytics - follow-up: embed reranker 5xx errors

Hey Marissa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and the issue we started hitting after integrating the SDK and switching our reranker over to the Redwood endpoint.

What we did:
- Integrated the Redwood Node SDK (v1.4.2) per the quickstart.
- Auth: Bearer token from our FinLytics account.
- Rerank flow: call /v1/embeddings to get vectors, then POST to /v1/rerank with embedding payloads in batches of ~120 items.

Observed problem: starting yesterday afternoon we began getting intermittent 502/504/500-ish responses from the rerank endpoint. Typical response is a 504 gateway timeout after ~20s. We attached a trimmed request log with request ids and times (finlytics-request-log.json). One sample failing request:

POST /v1/rerank
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>
{
  "model": "redwood-reranker-1",
  "items": [ ... ~120 embeddings ... ],
  "query_embedding": [ ... ]
}

Notes: reducing the batch to ~20 items seemed to reduce frequency but did not eliminate the problem. We also tried increasing client-side timeout to 30s with no consistent improvement.

Can you advise on:
1) Immediate mitigation we can apply on our side to stop the outages for production traffic.
2) What logs/IDs you need from us to triage (we included request ids in the attached log).
3) Whether this looks like a payload-size/batching problem or something server-side (routing/load balancing?)

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Price
Head of Integrations, FinLytics

---

Hi Jordan —

Appreciate the detailed recap and the logs. We're on it. Quick next steps from my side:

- Can you send one full raw request (headers + body) for a failing call with the request id visible? That will help with matching traces.
- In the meantime, try two quick mitigations on your side:
  1) Reduce max batch size to 50 items and re-run a few requests.
  2) Increase client-side timeout to 45s (to rule out transient backend slowness).

Technical note / potential quick fix (SDK config):
If you're on the Node SDK, you can set the request timeout and batch size like this: 

// Node SDK sample (quick test)
const client = new Redwood({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY,
  timeoutMs: 45000,      // increase socket timeout to 45s
  maxBatchSize: 50       // temporary: reduce batch size
});

If that reduces errors, it points at either per-request processing time or an intermediate gateway dropping large/chunked payloads.

I've looped in Camila (serving runtime) to try to reproduce from our side. I'll also open a support ticket with SRE if we see a clear pattern.

I'll follow up as soon as Camila has repro steps.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinLytics - follow-up: embed reranker 5xx errors

Hi all —

I pulled the attached sample log and ran a series of repros against our staging reranker endpoints using the same SDK version and a synthetic dataset modeled after FinLytics payloads. Summary so far:

Findings:
- I can reproduce a 502/504 when the combined request payload exceeds ~3.5MB and when the client uses HTTP/2 with chunked requests from behind certain proxies.
- The server logs show an upstream "idle connection" between our frontend load balancer and the backend worker that times out and tears down the stream, which the gateway surfaces as a 504.
- When I shrink the batch_size to <=50 items or reduce embedding dimension by truncating metadata, the failures stop consistently.

Repro steps (direct curl against our staging endpoint):
1) Prepare embeddings.json with ~120 base64 vectors (~3.8MB).
2) curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST https://staging.redwood.com/v1/rerank --data-binary @embeddings.json
3) Observe 504 at ~20s in staging (request id: staging-req-20260721-17).

Temporary mitigations we recommend to FinLytics:
- Reduce maxBatchSize to 40-50 until we roll a server fix.
- Disable HTTP/2 on the client/tracing proxy or set Connection: close to avoid chunked transfer heuristics that some proxies mishandle.
- Keep client timeout >= 45s while we investigate.

Longer-term: SRE will adjust the load-balancer upstream idle timeout and add a more forgiving retry path for long requests. I'm escalating to Sean to open the SRE ticket.

CC: Jordan, please try the two mitigations (batch size and disabling HTTP/2) and paste one failing request id if it still fails.

Camila Reyes
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachment: redwood-sdk-sample.patch (sample HTTP/1.1 client flags)
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@finlytics.com>

Date: 2026-07-22T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinLytics - follow-up: embed reranker 5xx errors

Thanks Camila — helpful repro notes. We applied both mitigations this morning:
- Reduced batch_size to 40 in production.
- Disabled HTTP/2 in our edge proxy.
- Increased client-side timeout to 60s.

Result: error rate dropped by ~85%, but we still observed occasional 504s under heavy traffic. One recent failing request id is req_20260722_2387 (log attached).

Can you share an ETA for the SRE change? Also, do you recommend we move reranking requests to a separate worker pool to avoid interfering with other realtime calls?

Appreciate the responsiveness — Jordan
Jordan Price
Head of Integrations, FinLytics

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-07-25T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinLytics - follow-up: embed reranker 5xx errors

Hi team —

SRE update and next steps. Thanks for the repro and request ids (req_20260722_2387). We've opened JIRA-INC-4321 to track the upstream idle-timeout and retry-policy changes. Preliminary root cause analysis:
- The frontend load balancer had a default upstream idle timeout of 30s which in combination with chunked uploads and certain proxy configs caused the upstream to close the connection during long-running rerank requests.

Planned fix and ETA:
- Increase upstream idle timeout to 90s and enable conservative retries for 5xx on the rerank route. Target: deploy config change to staging within 24 hours and to prod within 48 hours, pending roll validation.

Recommended customer actions (FinLytics):
1) Keep batch_size <= 50 while we validate the change.
2) Keep client timeout >= 60s for the next 72 hours.
3) Optionally route large rerank jobs to a background worker pool (we can help with the design).

I'll update JIRA-INC-4321 with logs and our validation checklist. Marissa, please share any contractual/SLAs notes with Jordan if FinLytics needs committed uptime during the rollout window.

Next communication: I'll post validation results to the JIRA ticket and tag you both.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Support & SRE Liaison, Redwood Inference
